$comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the time-sensitive facts about Moses Kolleh Sesay.
The same employment dates, degrees, certifications and profile links were
written out by hand in index.html, its JSON-LD block, field-report.html, the
narration scripts, the README and the CV. Six copies of a fact is six chances
for them to disagree, and they already had: field-report.html listed a
certification the rest of the site did not.
npm run build:content generates from this file: the JSON-LD block and the
at-a-glance strip in index.html, sitemap.xml (from `pages`), the Assay's
facts block in modules/interactives.js (roles, degrees and `languages`),
and the closing call to action on every page but the homepage (the email,
the CV and atAGlance.targetRoles); build:check fails in CI if any of them
is behind. The rest of the editorial pages is not generated from it —
index.html and field-report.html stay hand-authored outside those regions —
so tests/content.test.js reads this file and fails if any page disagrees
with it. Edit here first, run npm run build:content, then make the pages
match; the test tells you which ones are behind.
`verifiedOn` is the date a human last confirmed the ongoing facts (the
'Present' role in particular) were still true. The test prints a loud notice
$knowsAbout: Feeds JSON-LD. Keep it to areas with case-study evidence behind them — a schema.org claim is still a claim.
$languages: Optional and deliberately absent: add "languages": [{ "language": "Dutch", "level": "B1" }], named in English with a CEFR level (A1-C2) or "native", once Moses states them. Until then the Assay on the homepage lists every non-English language a job ad asks for as a gap rather than guessing. npm run build:content copies it into modules/interactives.js, and into the at-a-glance strip below.
$atAGlance: The strip under the homepage hero's copy: what a recruiter checks first.
npm run build:content writes it into index.html between the AT-A-GLANCE
markers. A fact that is null is not shown at all: no 'TBC', no placeholder,
and the validator refuses one written as a value. Only Moses can state
seniority, availableFrom and rightToWork (docs/owner-checklist.md, F2 and
F3). Two facts are read from elsewhere in this file rather than repeated:
languages (the top-level list above, the one the Assay reads) and the
location (person.locality and person.country).
targetRoles   required; the hero's availability line, after 'Open to '
workArea      optional; phrases on the same line, after the roles: where
he would work, which is a preference, not a right to work
seniority     a short phrase: the level of role sought
availableFrom 'now', or a date as YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD
rightToWork   a short phrase: where he may work, and whether an employer
would need to sponsor a visa
Short is a number: at most 80 characters for targetRoles, 32 for
seniority and for workArea (joined), 48 for rightToWork and 80 for the
languages as the strip writes them. On a phone the strip, the buttons
and the hero's figures share one screen; smoke.js checks the longest
strip these allow still fits (GLANCE_LIMITS in scripts/lib/content.js).

atAGlance.targetRoles: sustainability, climate-risk, ESG and sustainable-AI roles and consulting

currentRole.$comment: The one fact on the site with an open end date. Everything else is closed and cannot rot.
currentRole.title: Researcher — Sustainable Artificial Intelligence

$figures: A figure on a page needs a basis in content/. A case-study result carries its own; a record fact about a role or a degree (a team's headcount, a programme's length, a grade) sits on the entry it describes, here, and tests/content.test.js holds the pages to it. An outcome rate (a completion percentage, an efficiency gain, people reached) is not a record fact: it needs a method, and without one it stays off the site.

$certifications: The homepage's certificates (between the CERTIFICATES markers in
index.html) and the CV are printed from this list: name, issuer, date and
`covered`, one line on what it covered.
verifyUrl is optional and absent until Moses supplies it: the issuer's
own page for this certificate (Coursera's for the Google one, CFI's
credential site for theirs). With one, the homepage and the CV link it
as 'Verify'. Leave the field out rather than writing null or 'TBC' —
the build refuses a placeholder, and an address that is not https or
not on an issuer's host (VERIFY_HOSTS in scripts/lib/content.js).
